review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for the lemma names and for the `Icc ⌈a⌉₊ ⌊b⌋₊` shape. The only related declaration I found is `Nat.preimage_cast_Icc` in Algebra/Order/Floor/Semiring.lean, which is the set-preimage form of the same fact. None of the 16 lemmas carries `@[simp]`. I do not think that is a defect. Each lemma's right-hand side is a `Finset` or `Set` membership that simp would expand with `Finset.mem_Ioc` and the like. That would reduce it to floor/ceil inequalities, and the existing floor/ceil `le_floor`/`floor_lt`/`ceil_le`/`lt_ceil` lemmas would then normalise those further. Making these lemmas simp would add rules that overlap with that machinery without giving a canonical normal form. Several `Nat` lemmas also need side conditions (`0 ≤ a`, `0 ≤ b`) that simp would have to discharge. The proofs call `simp [floor_lt, le_floor]`, so they depend on the existing simp set and no loop is apparent. The deprecated `cast_mem_Ioc_iff'` alias is harmless for simp. I did not run Lean, so the simp-normal-form reasoning above is by inspection only.
